g.text: DRY-RUN mode: no changes will be made on HackerOne.
• The whole PoC uses `curl -I`, which only fetches headers. No response body was ever
captured, so nothing was actually shown to be disclosed.
OK from a health endpoint is expected. Load balancers use them.
• The reporter's own Impact section says
all closed as Informative or Not Applicable.
Public static assets, no sensitive files.
Thanks for your submission. The PoC relies on `curl -I`, which only returns headers, and
a 200 OK on a health endpoint is intentional: it's there for our load balancers. To be
actionable, an information disclosure needs to show sensitive data in the response body,
and the report itself says none is exposed. Closing as Informative. If you can show real
sensitive content, we're happy to take another look.
